name: Mindset
what: A daily motivation app that wakes you up with famous speeches, with streaks and leaderboards.
title: Mindset reached $24K a month by building on its team's YouTube audience first
dek: The people behind some of YouTube's biggest motivation channels built an app for the same audience. It took years, not months, and the YouTube audience did the heavy lifting.
pattern: Build the audience first, then the app

numbers.k: MRR (money coming in each month from subscriptions)
numbers.label: Verified

cost_to_start.label: Claimed

first_revenue.text: Not public. Speeches were free to play at launch in 2020. TrustMRR's verified numbers start in December 2025 at $17,629.
first_revenue.label: Claimed

first_customers.short: Listeners of the founders' YouTube motivation channels
first_customers.text: Listeners of the founders' own YouTube motivation channels. "Thousands of listeners" tested the app for months before the official launch.
first_customers.label: Claimed

team.label: Sources differ

phases.name: YouTube first
phases.story: One of the co-founders started a motivational speech channel on YouTube in 2016 as a side hobby. One of his first videos got a million views in its first month. He built more channels after that, including one for students.

number.v: 1 million views in the first month
number.label: Claimed

phases.lesson: An audience you build for free can become the first customers of anything you make later.

phases.name: Testing quietly
phases.story: The app went on the App Store in January 2020, but the team didn't announce it yet. Thousands of listeners tested it for months first. By then the team had deals with more than 20 YouTube channels to use their speeches, and a royalty system to pay those creators.
phases.lesson: Let real users test before the big launch. Fix what they hate while few people are watching.

phases.name: The official launch
phases.story: On November 15, 2020, the team announced Mindset as an app from "the world's biggest motivational YouTube network". They said the partner channels had over 13 million subscribers combined. At first, the speeches were free to play.
phases.lesson: If you already have an audience, a launch is just telling them where to go next.

phases.name: Slow, steady growth
phases.story: In March 2022 the app added Skills: you earn points and level up in eight life areas. By May 2022 it had passed 100,000 users and about 300,000 audio plays a month. That's roughly a year and a half after launch, even with a huge YouTube audience.
phases.lesson: Even with a head start, expect years of building, not weeks.

phases.name: Alarms, streaks and subscriptions
phases.story: Today the app leads with an alarm clock that wakes you to a famous speech, plus streaks, widgets and leaderboards. It charges $4.99 a week, $9.99 a month or $59.99 a year. MRR means monthly recurring revenue: money that comes in every month from subscriptions. Mindset's is $24,251. A month's revenue can be higher, because it counts all money collected that month, including yearly plans paid up front. Revenue moves between about $16,000 and $35,000 a month.

number.v: $35,034 in Sep 2026, the best month shown
number.label: Verified

phases.lesson: Features that bring people back every day, like an alarm or a streak, are what keep a subscription alive.

checklist: Pick one topic you could post about every week for a year, and post the first one this week.
Look at which of your posts or videos people save or share the most. That's the thing they'd pay for.
Ask five people who follow you what they'd want in an app or tool about that topic.
Give early testers free access and ask them one question: what almost made you stop using it?
If you use other people's content, get permission and agree how they get paid before you launch.
Add one reason to open your app every day (an alarm, a streak, a daily pick) and see if people come back.
